newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan synthetic stocks seen weak in near term.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan synthetic stocks seen weak in near term.

text.p: Pakistan's synthetic stocks should remain under pressure in the third quarter of 1997 after domestic fibre prices slumped to a four-year low, a research report said on Tuesday.
Local manufacturers reduced the price of polyester staple fibre by 2.0 rupees to 63 rupees per kg on July 1.

The cut was made because of over-supply after the commissioning of Ibrahim Fibre and ICI's expansion and also due to a sharp reduction in international fibre prices, a research note by the BMA Capital Market Management said.
"This year's estimated production of polyester staple fibre is around 290,000 tonnes compared to a demand of 270,000 tonnes in 1996," said Shoaib Saleem, an analyst at the BMA.
Despite the 20 percent growth in the consumption of local fibre in 1996 and an estimated 18 percent in 1997, fibre production would remain higher than its demand, he said.
He said after the commissioning of new plants, the domestic production capacity would be well over 360,000 tonnes.
The note said current international fibre prices at 89 or 90 cents per kg were the lowest in last six to seven years and there was little sign of an improvement in the rates because of over-supply.

BMA said local fibre industry's trouble had increased as imported fibre was cheaper, with its landed cost at the current duty structure coming to around 57 rupees per kg against the prevaling local market rate of 63 rupees.
Local fibre rates are likely to ease further in coming months, hitting earnings of local companies, Saleem said.
The report said the local industry's problems had been compounded after an increase in world prices of raw material.
"PTA (pure terephthaloc acid) price for the third quarter 1997 is being quoted at $640 per tonne (C&F) as compared to $625 per tonne in the second quarter, it said.

"The fibre stock prices have failed to move up despite a bullish rally over the last couple of weeks due to these negative developments. We envisage fibre stocks prices to remain weak in the coming months on the back of falling fibre prices."
